inspection_summary: Inspected all 3,343 splitlines of the normalized primary paper. The source develops a contradiction from Λ<0: complex-height asymptotics give zero counts, the backward-heat zero ODE drives a renormalized Hamiltonian toward local arithmetic-progression equilibrium, localized energy propagation transfers integrated control to time zero, and known zeta-zero gap statistics contradict the resulting concentration. The text layer is coherent enough for all accepted mechanisms, although displayed formula typography remains representation-dependent.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines H_t and states the de Bruijn–Newman boundary and the local-equilibrium contradiction in compressed form.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction and notation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Relates H_0 to ξ, introduces backward heat flow and Λ, contrasts the finite Lehmer-pair route with relaxation to local equilibrium, outlines the proof, and fixes zero indexing and asymptotic notation.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Asymptotics of H_t
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Obtains complex-height bounds and logarithmic-derivative asymptotics through heat-kernel transfer, saddle-point recentering, Stirling analysis, and dominance of the first Fourier mode.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Riemann–von Mangoldt type formulae
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines classical zero locations, proves their spacing, and transfers global and mesoscopic zero counts to H_t using the argument principle and a limiting-profile argument.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Dynamics of zeroes
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the repulsive zero ODE, explains the local-equilibrium timescale, and derives finite-subsystem Hamiltonian, energy, virial, and cross-energy identities.

sections_inspected.label: 5. A weak bound on gaps
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Propagates any extremely small gap through enlarging index intervals until macroscopic zero spacing forces a contradiction, yielding a quantitative gap lower bound.

sections_inspected.label: 6. A weak bound on integrated energy
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses spatial pigeonholing and the truncated Hamiltonian identity to obtain polynomial integrated-energy control needed for later interchange arguments.

sections_inspected.label: 7. Strong control on integrated energy
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Renormalizes energy and Hamiltonian relative to classical locations, localizes them smoothly, proves an approximate dissipation identity with negligible errors, establishes coercivity, and derives strong integrated-energy decay.

sections_inspected.label: 8. Controlling the energy at time 0
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Finds a good spatial interval and applies a Bourgain-style local propagation inequality over short time steps to turn averaged energy control into time-zero control.

sections_inspected.label: 9. Contradicting pair correlation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Converts small renormalized nearest-neighbor energy into concentration at mean spacing and contradicts a positive proportion of smaller zeta-zero gaps.

sections_inspected.label: References
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic support only; no standalone semantic units selected.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Complex-height asymptotics as a zero-density transfer channel
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Sharp control of H_t away from the real axis can be compressed into both macroscopic and mesoscopic zero-density information, with compactness recovering the finer scale that direct argument estimates do not.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The transfer is proved only under Λ<t≤0 and at the logarithmic height/resolution supported by the saddle estimates; it is not a general zero-counting principle for arbitrary entire functions.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From repulsive zero flow to localized equilibrium dissipation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The formal gradient-flow intuition becomes rigorous after subtracting the slowly varying classical lattice, smoothly truncating interactions, proving approximate dissipation, and coupling it with coercivity.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The reference lattice is not an exact equilibrium and the conclusion depends on a tailored nearby-pair cutoff and error scale; no unqualified global convexity theorem is established.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Small-gap control is the analytic-enablement layer
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A weak but subpolynomial gap lower bound, amplified to polynomial integrated-energy control, is sufficient to justify differentiating an infinite interaction functional even though it is far from the final equilibrium estimate.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The bounds are deliberately nonoptimal and are used for legality and domination, not as direct evidence of mean spacing.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Average dissipation reaches a statistical obstruction through buffered propagation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Smooth time-averaged energy control can be transferred to a terminal local block by selecting buffered spatial boundaries and iterating short-time monotonicity, after which nearest-neighbor statistics provide the contradiction.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The final obstruction uses an external theorem about zeta-zero gaps under the already implied Riemann hypothesis; this source does not reprove that statistical result.
